chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is Umar ibn Muslim doing?' I said: 'May I be your sacrifice! He has devoted himself to worship and abandoned trade.' He said: 'Woe to him! Does he not know that one who abandons the seeking (of livelihood) will not have his supplications answered?'

Indeed, a group from among the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when the verse was revealed: 'And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out, and He will provide for him from where he does not reckon,' they locked their doors and devoted themselves to worship, saying: 'We have been provided for.'

This reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and he sent for them and said: 'What drove you to what you have done?' They said: 'O Messenger of God! Our provisions were guaranteed for us, so we devoted ourselves to worship.' He said: 'Indeed whoever does that, his supplications will not be answered. You must seek (your livelihood).'

key_terms.الطَّلَب: Seeking/pursuit of livelihood; active effort to earn one's sustenance
key_terms.تَارِكَ الطَّلَبِ: One who abandons the seeking of livelihood; condemned for passivity
key_terms.لَا يُسْتَجَابُ لَهُ: His supplications are not answered; spiritual consequence of abandoning work
key_terms.مَخْرَجاً: A way out/an outlet; God's promise of relief to the God-fearing
key_terms.وَيْحَهُ: Expression of pity or rebuke: 'woe to him', indicating strong disapproval

ai.seo_question: Does abandoning work for worship mean supplications will not be answered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rebukes the misunderstanding that Quranic promises of divine provision excuse abandoning worldly work. Through a historical precedent from the Prophet's time, the Imam clarifies that even though God promises sustenance to the God-fearing, this divine promise requires active effort — one who abandons seeking livelihood will not have his supplications accepted. The hadith addresses a recurring misreading of Quran 65:2-3 that led some early Muslims to withdraw from trade and commerce, believing reliance on God meant passivity.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Haroun Bin Hamza, from Ali Bin Abdul Aziz who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘What does Umar Bin Muslim do?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! He has diverted towards the worship and neglects the business’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto him! The neglector of the seeking does not get his supplications Answered for him.

A group from the companions of Rasool-Allahsaww, when (the Verse) [65:2] and whoever is fearful of Allah, He will make for him an outlet [65:3] And He provides for him from (sources) he does not reckon, was Revealed, they locked their doors and diverted themselves towards the worship, and they were saying, ‘Allahazwj would Suffice for us’.

So that reached the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> sent for them. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What made you carry upon what you are doing?’ They said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! You<sup>saww</sup> guaranteed our livelihood for us, so we diverted ourselves towards the worship’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who does that, (his supplications) would not be Answered for him. It is upon you with the seeking (of the livelihood)’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from Muhammad ibn Ali from Harun ibn Hamzah from Ali ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once asked me, ‘What has ‘Umar ibn Muslim done?’ I replied, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, ‘he has devoted himself in worship and has given up doing any business.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Fie upon him! Does he not know that the prayer of one who neglects work to make a living is not answered?

A people of the companions of the Messenger of Allah, when this was revealed, “Those who maintain piety before Allah, He makes a way out for them and provides them sustenance from unexpected sources” [66:7], closed their doors and begun to worship. They said, “We have found what we needed.”

This was reported to the Holy Prophet who called them in his presence and asked, “What made you do what you had been doing?” They replied, O Messenger of Allah, you guaranteed our sustenance, and thus, we devoted ourselves in worship.” He said, “Whoever does this his prayer is not answered. You must work for your living.’””
